title: A boolean filter argument overwrites the existing filter on the same column
query: DEFINE MEASURE Sales[Red Sales] = CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], 'Product'[Color] = "Red" )
EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( 'Product'[Color], "Sales Amount", [Sales Amount], "Red Sales", [Red Sales] )

source.quote: The compact syntax (boolean) is expanded in the full syntax
source.supports: the page's first example runs this query on its own model: Red Sales shows the Red amount on every color row

source.quote: If the columns or tables are already in the filter context, the existing filters are overwritten by the new filters to evaluate the CALCULATE expression.
source.supports: a filter on a column already in the filter context is overwritten

source.quote: If all expressions evaluate to BLANK for a row, that row is not included in the table returned.
source.supports: the Green row is kept because Red Sales is not blank for it

derivation: Sales Amount: Red 460 (rows 1, 2, 3, 5, 7), Blue 80 (rows 4, 6), Green BLANK. Red Sales replaces the color filter of each row with Color = Red: 460 everywhere. Green has a non-blank Red Sales, so SUMMARIZECOLUMNS returns its row.
notes: SUM of a fixed decimal (currency) column is taken to be a fixed decimal, as in the seed cases.
